summary: Read the header and closing sections of both files, and surveyed the body of the larger one, checking declaration density. free-unification.lean (2231 lines) is a semantic framework plus a free-unification proof calculus: classes State/APatt/Pattern, structures APattBody/Disjunction, a Theory/Symbol declaration interface with operator-law proofs (associativity/commutativity), a `c_unification_examples` namespace exercising a `unify`/`unify_complete` tactic on concrete pattern goals, and worked `example`/`theorem` declarations. laxtheorem.lean (666 lines) formalizes a `Lax` speculative-proof modality (PSigma-based, with condition/certify/ret/bind/mult/mono/strength) and uses it to build a finite-state model-checking proof (`modelCheckCondition`, `certifiedModel`, `globalSafety`) discharged against explicit `axiom`-stated transition-completeness facts for a worked example graph. Both are dense, genuine formal-mathematics content (188 and 101 declaration-keyword hits respectively), matching the prior review's characterization of this source as symbolic model-checking and pattern-narrowing formalization.
